# Memory and memory import (area `memory`)

What FERB remembers about the owner, how it is recalled within limits, and importing memory from other assistants.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **MEM-1** (owner): FERB keeps the owner fact store. Procedure learning is replaced by a short "how I did it" note on each verified episode, retrieved by search for similar requests.
- **MEM-2** (owner): Forgetting a fact deletes the fact, its versions and its watcher-captured sources (trail rows), and blocks it from being re-learned. The owner's chat message that stated it stays: chat history is the owner's own record. FERB's past answers and traces are not scrubbed.
- **MEM-3** (owner): For memory, the owner's pass verdict counts as verified, as the checker's pass does; the owner's fail overrides the checker. The owner's latest verdict decides.
- **MEM-5** (owner): Memory has three tiers. Tier 1, the core profile, is always on in every role's prompt within a hard budget (about 2-3k tokens). Tier 2, the versioned fact store, holds everything. Tier 3 holds verified episodes with their how-notes, and playbooks. Everything outside Tier 1 is retrieved within limits, so prompts don't grow with memory.
- **MEM-6** (owner): Memory retrieval fuses a local embedding model running on the Mac with keyword search (bm25); the same search serves facts, episodes and old chat.
- **MEM-7** (owner): A change to a fact in the profile updates the profile at once, by code, with no model. A weekly model pass (sooner when over budget) compacts it: the model chooses and groups entries, code renders them from the facts, so the owner's words are never paraphrased.
- **MEM-8** (owner): The planner's remember rule and the daily distill's chat pass capture durable facts about the owner said in passing, not only after "remember ...". A fact FERB paraphrases is saved as FERB's understanding (MEM-12).
- **MEM-9** (owner): No special exclusion of health or finance facts in the planner or the distill. Secrets are masked by redaction as always.
- **MEM-10** (owner): Code stores what a remembered quote is about (from the task) next to the owner's exact words, so a line like "ok. score this 1 star - not ordering this again" still makes sense later. The words themselves are never reworded.
- **MEM-11** (owner): Forgetting a person or site also removes it from the known destinations, so a send to it asks again.
- **MEM-12** (owner): FERB saves facts itself, what the owner states and what it works out, each labelled by origin (the owner's words / FERB's understanding / observed). No Keep/Edit/Drop questions: a quiet "Memory: noted ..." line the owner can ignore or correct by talking. Memory never authorizes an action. A memory page in the app shows and edits everything.
- **MEM-13** (owner): From installed apps and their usage FERB works out what the owner mostly does, their most-used apps, main browser and main profile/account in it; it shows that once as "here's what I saw: ..." (no yes/no loop), stores it as observed facts, and refreshes it as usage changes. What holds up is promoted into Tier 1.
- **MEM-14** (owner): FERB's own understanding and observed facts that look over are retired automatically and the owner is told once. The owner's own words are retired automatically only when their recorded end date passes; otherwise FERB tells the owner once "this looks over, I'll stop using it", stops using it, keeps it as history, and restores it when the owner says it still holds.
- **MEM-17** (agent): PROFILE_TOKENS = 2,500 (within MEM-5's about 2-3k), counted as FERB's context counts (4 characters a token). Every render stops at the budget; what is left out is counted in one line and makes the profile pass due.
- **MEM-20** (agent): The pass runs weekly, or sooner when over budget, at most one try an hour; an owner fact that doesn't fit makes it due early, at most once in 24 h (EARLY_PASS_HOURS). The model returns sections of ids and `ended`; code refuses ids that don't hold up, renders every entry word for word, retires the ended ones ("FERB's weekly check") and tells the owner once in chat.
- **MEM-21** (agent): The planner looks up similar existing facts when a new one may replace one (memory.read, ORCH-515; Tier 1's facts are in its prompt) and names any a new fact replaces (`replaces`, ids checked by code); the "Memory: noted" line names what was replaced. A version resting on the owner's words now ends every current version of its fact and the named ids that hold; any other version never ends one the owner stated. Identical words are credited to the existing item (the owner's first), never a twin.
- **MEM-22** (agent): The daily distill stays (one call a day). Its retire on the owner's words (passing `_may_end`) or on its own check is applied and told once, no Retire/Keep question; words older than the item are refused. A stored key is skipped unless the owner's quote replaces it. Items due for a check (`review_at`) are listed to it; one it doesn't retire has its date cleared.
- **MEM-23** (agent): A known destination goes when its stored value is whole words of the forgotten item's content, label or subject name; a host also by its bare host or its site label (4+ letters: "kaggle" for www.kaggle.com); a phone by its digits (6+). The "Forget for good?" list says which.
- **MEM-25** (agent): The embedding model is minishlab/potion-base-8M (MIT, pinned revision and SHA-256s), a static table (29,528 WordPiece tokens x 256 float32; a text = the normalized mean of its tokens' rows), read by FERB's own tokenizer and memory-mapped safetensors: no numpy, torch, MLX or onnxruntime. Its vocabulary is English-only; other languages and coined words fall back to keywords.
- **MEM-26** (agent): The model files ship in FERB.app (Contents/Resources/models/embeddings/<name>@<rev12>) and are read there, never fetched by the app; a checkout's setup fetches them at install into ~/.ferb/models/embeddings (temporary folder, hashes checked, then renamed); `[memory] embedding_model` can name a folder. Until the model is there, search runs on keywords and recency. Tests never download.
- **MEM-27** (agent): Worker and plan step: facts + learned items <= 2,000 tokens and <= 10 items, no pushed chat, today's activity <= 2,000 tokens. The background attention check (tool-less): facts + learned items <= 4,000 tokens and <= 20 items (search.ATTENTION). The planner is pushed no memory, chat or activity (2026-11-03, ORCH-515): it looks them up. What doesn't fit is one counted line naming memory.read / memory.learned / trail.query. Lookup tools rank at most 100.
- **MEM-29** (agent): Code groups verified cards by goal similarity (PLAYBOOK_SIMILARITY 0.5); one model call says same kind or not and writes the steps; code checks the ids. At most 3 merges an hourly pass, only while no task runs, at most the 6 newest runs per call. A playbook is rewritten as new runs join; the owner's edit is never replaced; a declined group is not asked again.
- **MEM-30** (agent): A card keeps every episode, journal and memory ref, and one ref per distinct origin set of the others; its origin labels are computed from all refs.
- **MEM-31** (agent): A how-note is built from the worker's `how`, the owner's hints to the running task (quoted with their origin, 300 characters each) and the steps the card's recorded tool calls show (at most 12 steps, 600 characters). It is shown for verified runs only.
- **MEM-32** (agent): An owner fact that looks over (MEM-14) is set aside in `memory_set_aside`, beside memory_items: out of prompts, search and the profile at once, kept as history, restored when the owner says the same words again or by memory.restore. The login username it gave stays (it is still theirs and current).
- **MEM-33** (agent): Every turn records the memories it was given (`context.exposure`), so a repeated owner correction ("I told you before") traces to a memory miss and repeat runs show whether a how-note or playbook was used.
- **MEM-34** (agent): memory_items is the source of truth for facts, versioned, with source and validity window. No fact or identity copies live in learning_nodes. Facts tied to a period carry an end date (`until`) or a review date (`review_in_days`).
- **MEM-35** (owner): The owner's own words join Tier 1 at once only when they are about the owner. What the owner says about other things is placed by the weekly profile pass like any other fact.
- **MEM-400** (owner): FERB imports what matters about the owner from the major AI assistants they use (web, CLI and Mac apps), with schema-based extraction per assistant. Accuracy and recall are what count, and many model calls are acceptable; the result must make sense in FERB's memory and actually help it.
- **MEM-401** (owner): The import reads only the last 3 months of each assistant's transcripts, usage and saved memory; anything older is not read.
- **MEM-402** (owner): Every imported fact is saved as FERB's understanding (`inferred`), never as the owner's own words, and an import never adds known destinations.
- **MEM-403** (owner): The import reads ChatGPT and claude.ai from their data exports (web and Mac app, saved memories and projects where the export has them), Claude Code and Codex CLI from local transcripts on this Mac, and Gemini from Google Takeout.
- **MEM-404** (owner): The import extracts facts, preferences, projects, people and recurring tasks (as FERB's understanding); the raw imported chats are held in memory only while read, never stored or made searchable.
- **MEM-405** (owner): Extraction runs on the configured AI service; texts are redacted before they leave the reader module, and storage stays on the Mac.
- **MEM-406** (owner): No Keep questions and no batch review: imported facts show on the Memory page (filterable by source) and in one summary notice, and join the core profile only once they hold up. Since they rest on the import day's journal row, in practice that is after a week uncorrected or when the owner says it again.
- **MEM-407** (agent): Owner lines are: ChatGPT `user`, claude.ai `human`, Gemini "Prompted" records, Claude Code typed turns (not meta, sidechain, tool result or compact summary; `turnOrigin` human where present; no SDK sessions or subagent files), Codex interactive sessions only (`source` cli/vscode). Custom instructions and claude.ai project instructions count; uploaded files, attachments and tool output are not read; injected tag blocks are dropped.
- **MEM-408** (agent): Recall candidates are kept only when they cite an owner message (or a saved-memory claim) with a quote that is whole words of it; a verifier's supported verdict is kept only when its quote is whole words of an owner message shown as evidence. Saved memories (ChatGPT, claude.ai, Claude Code) are claims: kept only when the verifier cites an owner message of that source. An undated claude.ai memory is dated as of the import, its owner words still within the window.
- **MEM-409** (agent): Facts merge by `same_as` or kind+subject+key, oldest first. Newer wins by when the owner said it (`memory_import_items.said_at`, else a held fact's save time): an older imported version is skipped, not inserted as history. A fact the owner stated in their own words is never replaced or duplicated by an import (counted `kept_owner`). `ended`/`until` set an expiry; `review_in_days` a review.
- **MEM-410** (agent): Each conversation part's hash is recorded when done (`memory_import_done`), in the same step its facts are saved, so re-importing the same export later reads only what is new and a restart resumes. A forgotten fact is never re-imported (its fingerprint).
- **MEM-411** (agent): Every import model call (recall and each verify) waits while a chat turn runs (`_wait_idle` inside `_call`); running tasks don't block it. Three failed chunks in a row stop the run ("failed", told once); a later start goes on.
- **MEM-412** (agent): Import calls use the worker runtime with no tools and typed output (as the distill and profile pass). Their spans are `model.learning` with roles `memory_import_recall`/`memory_import_verify` and the goal "import memory from <assistant>", never the input. The estimate says 2 × chunks model calls; the run's actual count is in `counts.model_calls`.
- **MEM-413** (agent): Texts are cut at a word boundary, the cut said in the text: an owner message at 6,000 chars, an assistant reply at 700 (it only corroborates), a saved memory at 6,000. A recall call reads chunks of about 24,000 chars; a verification call batches about 30,000.
- **MEM-414** (agent): Gemini Takeout records whose marker word isn't the English "Prompted" are not read; the JSON variant with `details` Request is. Gemini HTML times in a zone other than UTC/GMT are read in this Mac's zone.
- **MEM-415** (owner): Memory import covers ChatGPT, claude.ai, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini; no other assistants are added for now.
- **MEM-416** (agent): A fact that only a running task's targets name (the permit task's username) is recalled into that task's worker and plan steps within their memory limits (2026-11-03: planner turns are pushed no memory and look it up, ORCH-515), with the parent task's goal shown above a step's own, even among many past tasks that share the goal's words.
- **MEM-417** (agent): The developer memory dashboard serves only requests that carry its token from its own origin and host; anything else is refused.
- **MEM-418** (agent): The episode card reader takes no arguments and opens only the database of the FERB home it finds itself; a request naming another home, or none, is refused.
- **MEM-419** (owner): What a memory capture saves as the owner's words is only the part of their message that states the fact, never the whole message: the planner's content and quote are those words (with any negation or condition that belongs to them), and code saves the owner's own spelling of that span.
- **MEM-420** (agent): items.owner_clauses saves, from the owner's words, the clause(s) that hold the planner's content as whole words: from the clause mark before it to the one after it (, ; : ! ? or a line break; never a period, so "prof." and "Dr." don't cut a clause). A negation or condition in the same clause stays; one a mark sets apart stays only when the content holds it, as the planner's prompt says. Replaces the re-review R5 rule that saved the whole line.
- **MEM-421** (agent): A day whose distillation failed stays in `pending_days`, so each hourly memory pass tries it again until it is distilled; no count limits the tries. Each failure is journaled `memory.distill_failed` with the day, the error and the attempts so far, and `doctor.check` lists the failed days (`learning.undistilled`), which `ferb doctor` shows. Replaces the old rule that parked a failed day until its summary changed or a `ferb memory distill DAY` that no longer exists.
- **MEM-422** (agent): An episode card that can't be built is still tried once more on the next hourly pass and, failed twice on the same inputs, waits for them to change (unchanged). Each failure is journaled `memory.cards_failed` with the task id, the error and what follows (tried once more, or waits until its task changes). `Learning.stuck_cards` lists the parked ones; `doctor.check` returns them as `learning.stuck_cards` and `ferb doctor` shows each. The pointer to a nonexistent `ferb memory consolidate` (and its unused `force`) is gone.
- **MEM-423** (owner): The Mac profile scan's facts (MEM-13) join Tier 1 at once when saved, within its budget, labelled observed. For everything else MEM-15 stands unchanged: The owner's own words join Tier 1 at once (same turn). FERB's understanding and observed facts join once they hold up (seen on 2 separate days, or standing 7 days uncorrected), and their join adds one quiet "Now always on: ... (label)" note card with Correct / Forget, never a question. The profile stays within its budget; the weekly pass only chooses and groups. The profile text is identical between turns unless a profile entry changed.
- **MEM-424** (agent): The owner's words hold up at once; so do the Mac profile scan's facts (MEM-423): observed items resting on a `memory.mac_profile` journal row, which only `mac_profile.store` writes (`Memory.from_mac_scan`), setup's scan and each weekly re-interpretation alike. FERB's other understanding and observed facts hold up once their sources span two separate days, or once they have stood a full weekly pass (7 days) without being replaced, retired or forgotten. An item kept under an older build's Keep question holds up at once; the old setup dump never does.
- **MEM-425** (agent): Code joins at once, under "Recently said" while it fits, only facts whose `subject` is "owner": the owner's words (MEM-35; not a fact placed by search, memory.search_only), the Mac scan's facts (MEM-423), and FERB's other understanding or observations once a save shows them holding up (a second day). The owner's words about anything else wait for the weekly pass, which places them like any fact. A join that isn't the owner's words adds its "Now always on" card. The pass is the only scheduled rewrite; the owner's pins survive it.
- **MEM-426** (agent): Code gathers the 25 most-used apps (TOP_APPS), installed/used counts, browsers and Chromium profiles; one model call (mac_profile.md) writes the summary and facts, stored observed and active at once, and in Tier 1 at once within its budget (MEM-423). Shown once (setup step, else one chat notice). Re-checked weekly with the profile pass; re-interpreted only when the 10 most-used apps, browsers or profiles changed (facts_fingerprint); a key not given again ends. A re-interpretation's facts are scan facts too: a new version takes its entry's place at once (MEM-7); a new key joins with its card.
